palette.notes: Code: 4 colours on the still (first 20 s measured); the clip mixes many flat-colour slides, screenshots and game footage, so no single palette. Slides use one flat background colour per tip.

lighting: Flat slide backgrounds; examples show a single-light portrait and a sphere lit from one side to teach shading.
silhouette: Simple icons per tip (robot, potion bottle, sphere, portrait) centred and readable at small size.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 16.7 ms, 19.93 changes/s over the first 20 of 55 s; fast cuts, one tip per ~3-4 s, with lines drawing on and check or question marks popping.

texture: Clean 2x pixel scale (native 288x512) on the drawn slides, no dithering; mixed with photo and screen captures.
camera: Static centred slides with cuts on every spoken word or tip; inserts of a website, a photo of a rabbit, game footage and a launcher.

acting.enters: Icons pop onto a flat colour background.
acting.acts: Comparisons: two potion bottles with question marks, then a tick on the better one; lines draw themselves.
acting.exits: Hard cut on the next word.
acting.depth: No depth; one centred object per slide.

techniques: one tip per slide, one flat background colour each
A/B comparison with a tick mark
line drawing itself on to show stroke rules
palette advice: use a ready-made list (Lospec)
single light source on a sphere to teach shading
feel: flat colour slide + one centred sprite + tick/question-mark pop = fast readable tips
for_fred: Use the A/B beat: show two versions side by side with question marks, then pop a tick onto the right one while Fred nods at it; one idea per 3-4 s slide.
